Run Python directly, without shell quoting. h is already praxis_hands: h.read, h.edit, h.write, h.search use the same editor, version checks and receipts. h.hand('name', **args) calls any hand in this turn's authorized catalogue through the live parent dispatcher, with its rights, durable receipts and Stop. r['outcome'] is the hand's own outcome (confirmed/refused/in_doubt/partial/ok/failed, unknown if it reports none); print r['content'] for its reply; r also has result_ref, call_id and image_count. h.describe('name')['content'] gives the full schema. InDoubt means check the receipt, never repeat the effect blindly. The bridge expires when this outer call returns or reaches its ceiling; a nested hand already started when the script stops waiting still finishes and its receipt follows [exit N]. Standalone workers/background survivors have no live bridge. Print results you need. cwd defaults to your local home, or the local Forge task root with task_id. Local task execution inherits custody and Stop; remote tasks are refused before execution. At home timeout=0 uses the configured shell default (normally 30s), capped at 600s; in a task 0 means unlimited. The output ends with [exit N]; a timeout closes the ordinary process group. Background descendants survive normal completion. Prefer h.edit to whole-file string replacement. To run one program with exact arguments, call run_command instead of subprocess glue.

Run one program with exact arguments and no shell: argv[0] is the program (PATH name or a path relative to cwd), every other item reaches it as one argument, byte for byte. Quotes, spaces, ;, $(), *, ~, backslashes and newlines are plain data, never expanded. Choose it for an ordinary program call (git show 'HEAD:a b.py', pytest -k x, ffmpeg ...); python for computation, loops or h; shell only when you want shell grammar (pipes, redirects, globs, &&, background &). It never falls back to shell. Routes: home (the Linux container, cwd defaults to /app, same rights and autocommit as shell) or, with task_id, a local Forge task (task root, admission, custody, Stop and its full log). Host and Windows tasks are refused before anything is sent: their backends take only shell strings; use coding_run there, or computer for the Windows laptop. At home timeout=0 uses the configured default (normally 30s), capped at 600s; in a task 0 means no deadline. stdin_text is sent exactly as UTF-8 then EOF; omitted means closed stdin. stdout and stderr arrive combined in one stream; the full output is kept. The reply ends with a [run_command {...}] facts line (executor, cwd, argv, resolved program, exit_code or signal, timed_out and tree_stop), [changes] and [exit N]. [exit unobserved] means no exit status was seen (timeout): never read it as success. refused: nothing was launched (bad argv, missing program or cwd). in_doubt: it may have run; check before repeating. A non-zero exit does not mean nothing changed. Optional env, outputs and scratch: see their fields; the facts line reports them.
Program then its arguments, one array item per argument
Working directory; home default /app, task paths are relative to the task root
Seconds; 0 uses the home default or no task deadline

Позвать руку из моего указателя по имени — СРАЗУ, по сигнатуре из указателя, без describe: например name="fs_read", args_json='{"path": "soul/SOUL.md"}' или name="coding_agent", args_json='{"task_id": "…", "action": "spawn", …}'. args_json — JSON-объект по её аргументам (пустой = без аргументов). Рука исполняется как родная: те же права, расписки, пределы и тот же результат. `describe` — только если сигнатуры мало (перечисления, вложенные объекты), один раз на ход.
имя руки из указателя
аргументы руки JSON-объектом, например {"path": "soul/SOUL.md"}
